title: Assessing occurrences, transformations, and source apportionment of nitrate in a riverine area (Southwestern China) using multi-parameter approaches
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhan Xie, Yunhui Zhang, Denghui Wei, Haidong Li, Lanchu Tao, Qingsong Chen, Juan Antonio Torres-Martínez, Rongwen Yao, Yangshuan Wang, Ying Wang
abstract: Study region Luolouhe (LLH) catchment in the western Yungui Plateau of southwestern China Study focus Investigating the transformation pathways and source apportionment of nitrate in regional riverine systems remains challenging due to spatial variations in topography, hydrogeology, and land use patterns. Thus, stable isotopes, the Bayesian stable isotope mixing model (MixSIAR), positive matrix factorization (PMF), and local indicators of spatial association (LIAS) were applied to elucidate the sources and contributions of nitrate (NO3 –). New hydrological insights for the region High NO3 – concentrations in surface water and groundwater were observed in the alluvial terrace in the LLH catchment. Nitrification was identified as the predominant biochemical process in both water bodies. Two water bodies in our study presented different nitrate sources. Nitrate source contributions ranked as domestic sewage and manure (DSM) (54.00% by SIAR and 62.15% by PMF)> chemical fertilizer (CF) (27.00% by SIAR and 25.51% by PMF)> soil nitrogen (SN) (17.70% by SIAR and 12.30% by PMF) in surface water. For groundwater, nitrate sources ranked as SN (52.40%)> CF (27.30%) > DSM (19.20%) by SIAR, while ranked as SN (58.74%)> DSM (21.43%)> CF (19.65%) by PMF. The non-perfect sewage discharge facilities and the surface runoff contributed to the nitrate sources in surface water. SN dominated the nitrate source due to the high background levels of nitrate in the soil profile. A proportion of nitrate fertilizer was transported into rivers while the rest percolated through the unsaturated zone and accumulated in the groundwater. The soil nitrate input hotspots identified by LISA further illustrated the spatial heterogeneity of the nitrification process. The hotspots scattered in the lower reach indicated an intense nitrification process in this region, facilitated by favorable oxidation conditions. Overall, this study enhances nitrate source apportionment methodologies and provides novel insights into the spatial variability of biochemical processes influencing nitrate concentrations at a regional scale.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of bed material grain size in the Lower Yellow River
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zipu Ma, Hongbo Ma
abstract: Study region The Yellow River Basin and the Lower Yellow River in China. Study focus Bed material grain size in the Lower Yellow River (LYR) has undergone substantial changes during 1963–2020, influenced by the dam operations, soil conservation, and water diversion. This study analyzed bed material data from seven hydrological stations along the LYR, comprising 398 groups of annual average grain size measurements. The median grain size, sorting parameter, and compositional variation of the grain size distribution sampled from the river bed of LYR were analyzed to identify the influencing factors on their spatial-temporal evolution. New hydrological insights for the region This study investigated the spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of bed material grain size in the Lower Yellow River (LYR). We found that (1) the median grain size (D 50 ) experienced three phases in the past: minimal change (1963–1985), significant decrease (1986–1999), and notable increase (2000–2020). Bed sediment grain size exhibited longitudinal fining along the river during all periods. The sorting coefficient (σ) remained stable over time but decreased along the river, indicating an enhanced size uniformity. Compositionally, fine sand(FS) and coarse silt(CS) exhibited opposing trends during 1986–1999 (decreasing FS and increasing CS) and 2000–2020 (increasing FS and decreasing CS), whereas very fine sand (VFS)remained relatively stable as the transitional component. (2) Dam construction, soil and water conservation, and water diversion substantially impacted bed material characteristics. The impoundment of the Longyangxia Reservoir caused the fining of downstream bed materials, reducing D 50 and fine sand while increasing coarse silt. In contrast, the construction of the Xiaolangdi (XLD) Reservoir caused coarsening. Soil and water conservation reduces sediment load at Tongguan station, increasing D 50 when sediment load is less than 5 × 10⁸t due to erosion and selective coarsening in the LYR, but without increasing the sorting coefficient. Declined stream runoff, combined with unchanged water diversion from 1986 to 1999, drove bed material fining. This provides a scientific basis and technical support for river regulation and engineering applications.

title: Mechanistic drivers and spatiotemporal thresholds of socioeconomic drought in the East River Basin, China: A causal-informed explainable AI approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Fangxiu Meng, Huazhou Chen, Yao Wang, Rong Wu, Lin Liu, Tao Tang, Shengzhi Huang, Jianfeng Li, Suning Liu, Haiyun Shi
abstract: Study region The East River Basin (ERB), a critical water source for South China’s mega-cities. Study focus To address data scarcity and the predictive collapse of traditional models during extreme deficits, this study develops an integrated diagnostic-predictive framework for the Distributed Standardized Socioeconomic Drought Index (DSSEDI). High-fidelity DSSEDI forecasting (maintaining a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.774 during extreme deficits) is achieved by leveraging accessible multi-source data, overcoming sector-specific monitoring constraints. By coupling a Causal Convolutional Transformer with Shapley Additive Explanations, the framework ensures physical consistency through dual-causal constraints. Crucially, incorporating a quantile regression loss function ( q = 0.5 ) significantly outperforms Mean Squared Error-based models in capturing non-Gaussian extreme drought peaks. New hydrological insights This analysis reveals the underlying socioeconomic drought mechanisms in the ERB, which exhibits a persistent climate memory characterized by 10- to 11-month hydrometeorological lags. A critical finding is the identification of a soil moisture paradox, where high antecedent moisture paradoxically accelerates drought development via enhanced evapotranspiration under urban heat island stress. Furthermore, the modeling framework implicitly diagnoses Xinfengjiang Reservoir regulation and exposes a pronounced socioeconomic antagonism, demonstrating that rigid industrial demand acts as a persistent drought amplifier. Distinct soil moisture inflection points (750 mm for urban and 600 mm for agricultural zones) are identified as scientific triggers for adaptive management. These findings establish a threshold-driven governance paradigm for enhancing drought resilience in urbanizing regional basins.

title: Regional hydrochemical assessment and trace-element screening in hail groundwater, Saudi Arabia
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Kamal Abdelrahman, Abdulaziz Saad Bin Osfur
abstract: Study Region Hail in northwestern Saudi Arabia is a hyper-arid, groundwater-dependent region where the regional Saq sandstone aquifer is hydraulically and geochemically influenced by Paleozoic cover rocks, Precambrian basement, local volcanic units and Quaternary wadi deposits. Salinity and geogenic trace constituents constrain the safe use of water. Study Focus Thirty regional water samples collected in December 2025 (28 groundwater wells and two surface-water reference sites) were evaluated for pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), turbidity, major ions, nutrients and trace/metalloid elements. Parameter-specific guideline screening, sodium adsorption ratio (SAR), GIS-based regional screening maps, Pearson correlation and principal component analysis (PCA) were integrated to identify hydrochemical domains and management priorities. New hydrological insights for the region The regional samples were neutral to alkaline (pH 7.29–10.32) and ranged from weakly mineralized to brackish (EC 90–9225 µS/cm; TDS 111–7600 mg/L). Twelve samples exceeded 1000 mg/L TDS and two exceeded the FAO severe irrigation-salinity threshold of 3.0 dS/m. SAR ranged from 0.15 to 18.31; 29 samples were S1 and GW-29 was S3. EC-TDS-Ca-Mg-Sr-Na-SO4 associations and PC1 (44.1%) define a robust salinity-hardness pathway driven by evaporation, carbonate/gypsum dissolution, ion exchange, and residence-time variation. PC2 (18.5%) separates reported Se-Sn-Sb-Si behavior from bulk salinity.

title: Lakeshore transformation and water color dynamics: A satellite-based 23-year assessment of nine plateau lakes in Yunnan, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yuchen Wang, Yongquan Zhao, Xuejun Duan, Xiao Zhang, Xunyi Pan
abstract: Study region Nine plateau lakes in Yunnan, China. Study focus We developed an extended lakeshore utilization classification framework to categorize lakeshores as natural, agricultural, or artificial using fixed maximum shorelines. We then derived the Forel–Ule Index (FUI) of the nine lakes from MODIS to characterize water color dynamics during 2000–2022. We quantified lakeshore composition and transformation trajectories, assessed FUI trends, and examined contemporaneous and one- and two-year lagged lakeshore–FUI associations. New hydrological insights for the region Lakeshore classification achieved 98.8% overall accuracy. Four lakes exhibit intensification, two show adjustment, and three remain relative stable. Artificial lakeshore increases from 29.1% to 45.2% in Erhai, while agricultural lakeshore increases from 36.3% to 73.5% in Chenghai. Significant upward FUI trends occur in Erhai, Chenghai, Yangzong, and Xingyun, whereas Lugu exhibits a downward trend and the other lakes show no significant trends. Contemporaneous lakeshore–FUI associations is significant for natural and artificial lakeshore in Erhai and Lugu and for agricultural lakeshore in Yilong, with none supported elsewhere. The lagged analysis shows that five lakeshore–FUI associations strengthen and five weaken. These contrasting responses indicate that lakeshore transformation alone does not determine water color dynamics, which is conditioned by lake-specific environmental and anthropogenic contexts. The proposed framework supports integrated lakeshore and water color monitoring and coordinated lake–watershed management in Yunnan and comparable lake systems.

title: Hierarchical ecohydrological controls on drought-driven ecosystem stability in alpine and temperate grasslands across the Qinghai–Tibetan and Mongolian plateaus
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yusi Zhang, Yuhai Bao, Zhonghua He
abstract: Study region This study examines alpine and temperate grasslands across the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau (TP) and the Mongolian Plateau (MP) during 2001–2023, representing two contrasting hydroclimatic settings in Asia. Study focus This study aims to compare drought regimes, drought-related ecosystem response patterns, and their associated climatic pathways between alpine and temperate grasslands. Seasonal-scale drought was identified using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index at a 3-month timescale (SPEI-3), and ecosystem stability was quantified from monthly satellite gross primary productivity (GPP) anomalies. Four complementary stability metrics were considered, including resistance (Ω), resilience (Δ), constraint time (Ct), and recovery time (Rt). Random-forest attribution and residual-based partial correlations were combined to assess both predictor importance and directional relationships. New hydrological insights for the region under study Temperate grasslands on the MP experienced stronger and more persistent drying, whereas alpine grasslands on the TP showed weaker and more spatially mixed drought trends. Consistent with these drought regimes, TP grasslands generally showed higher resistance and shorter Ct/Rt, while MP grasslands exhibited lower resistance but higher resilience and longer drought impacts. RF and partial-correlation analyses revealed a hierarchical contrast in climatic associations: TP stability was primarily linked to atmospheric demand and moisture–productivity coupling including vapor pressure deficit, soil water conditions, radiation and GPP, whereas MP stability was more strongly associated with energy-related conditions especially temperature and radiation, with atmospheric demand additionally shaping resilience. These findings indicate that drought-driven stability differs not only in magnitude but also in directional climatic associations, highlighting distinct drought buffering and post-drought recovery pathways across the two plateau systems.

title: A multi-scale evaluation of 30 empirical models for reference evapotranspiration estimation in a data-scarce semi-arid region: A case study of Jhansi, India
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Amit Kumar Singh, Ajay N. Satpute, Gaurendra Gupta, Avijit Ghosh, Samir Barman
abstract: Study region Semi-arid agro-climatic zone of central India. Study focus This study evaluated the performance of 30 empirical ET0 models; ten each from the temperature-based, mass-transfer-based and radiation-based categories, against the FAO-PM standard using 21 years (2000–2020) of daily meteorological observations at Jhansi, India. The analysis is framed as a benchmarking of empirical models against FAO-PM. Model accuracy was quantified at daily, monthly, seasonal and annual scales using four statistical indices (NSE, RMSE, MBE and r), and an integrated model ranking was derived using the entropy-weighted TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making framework. New hydrological insights for the region The 21-year FAO-PM record reveals a persistent annual atmospheric water deficit of ~731 mm (ET₀ = 1571 mm yr⁻¹ versus rainfall = 840 mm yr⁻¹). This deficit is highly asymmetric: the summer season alone (May–June) accounts for 440 mm of ET0 against negligible rainfall, defining the period of maximum irrigation demand, while the monsoon surplus is offset within weeks by rapid soil moisture depletion. Pre-winter and winter seasons contribute a further 295 mm of ET0. The leading models are wind-driven mass-transfer models, showing that aerodynamic demand rather than solar radiation is the primary control on daily ET₀ variability in this climate. Category alone, however, poorly predicts performance across the models. The Penman model (TOPSIS rank 1, closeness = 0.953) and WMO model (rank 2), requiring only wind speed and vapour pressure inputs, are identified as most accurate FAO-PM substitutes at the daily and seasonal scale. The findings of the study are location-specific and need validation before applying to other locations in the semi-arid region.

title: System-scale hydraulic trade-offs of dredging in confined urban rivers: Insights from the Tamsui basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Wan-Cheng Chen, Gene Jiing-Yun You, Gwo-wen Hwang, Jen-Yang Lin, Yu-Ju Hung
abstract: Study Region This study focuses on the Tamsui River Basin in northern Taiwan, a densely urbanized river system with limited channel expansion capacity and an extensive levee-floodway network designed for a 200-year flood standard. Study Focus This study evaluates dredging as a maintenance-based strategy for sustaining fixed flood-protection thresholds in space-constrained urban rivers where flood mitigation depends on coupled main-channel and floodway performance. A system-scale assessment using two-dimensional hydrodynamic and sediment-transport modeling examines how alternative dredging configurations influence hydraulic loading, diversion performance, and sediment adjustment under a representative 50-year flood event, with evaluation focused on a major urban bottleneck, the floodway inlet, and the downstream mainstem outlet. New Hydrological Insights for the Region The results show that dredging progressively alleviates hydraulic loading at the primary urban bottleneck, with greater relief achieved under more extensive interventions. However, simulations demonstrate that increased main-channel conveyance can reduce floodway diversion by weakening the hydraulic head driving bifurcation flow, confirming a diversion-conveyance trade-off in urban flood-routing systems. Sediment responses are strongly location-dependent, with rapid re-accumulation in confined metropolitan reaches and persistent scouring in the downstream mainstem. Together, these coupled hydraulic and sediment responses indicate that maintaining fixed flood-protection thresholds through maintenance-based dredging becomes increasingly difficult in space-constrained urban rivers.

title: Spatiotemporal heterogeneity and mechanisms of mountain-outlet runoff change on the northern slope of the Qilian Mountains during 1960–2020
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yuchen Wei, Meiping Sun, Xiaojun Yao, Shu Wang, Rongjun Wang, Shuting Niu
abstract: Study region Five major mountain-outlet basins on the northern slope of the Qilian Mountains, northwestern China: Shiyang (SY), Heihe (HH), Beida (BD), Shule (SL), and Danghe (DH). Study focus This study examines the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of mountain-outlet runoff changes during 1960–2020 and their statistically associated pathways using hydrological, meteorological, atmospheric circulation, glacier, and snow data. OPGD and PLS-SEM were used to identify dominant explanatory factors and statistical pathways linking atmospheric circulation, meteorological factors, glacier and snow water storage (GSWS), and runoff (Q). New hydrological insights for the region Mean runoff in 2000–2020 was 2.8–58.8% higher than in 1960–1999, while basin-specific abrupt-change years ranged from 1987 to 2009. Long-term increasing trends were significant only in HH, SL, and DH. Air temperature and precipitation were the main meteorological factors associated with runoff variation. Runoff in SY and HH was more closely associated with precipitation, whereas runoff in SL and DH was more closely associated with air temperature, and both factors had similar explanatory power in BD. Atmospheric circulation was statistically linked to runoff through air temperature, precipitation, and GSWS. The precipitation → Q pathway was stronger in SY, HH, and BD, whereas the air temperature → GSWS → Q pathway was more prominent in SL and DH. These findings help explain region-specific runoff heterogeneity and support differentiated water resources management.

title: Runoff response to terrace construction, vegetation restoration, and urban expansion: Case studies in the Yiluo and Upper Wei River basins
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Mingjie Yang, Yuanhong Liu, Peng Zhang, Saihua Liu, Lianqing Xue, Tao Lin
abstract: Study region This study investigates two typical semi-arid loess watersheds in China, the Yiluo River Basin and Upper Wei River Basin, where terrace renovation, vegetation restoration, and urbanization have substantially altered watershed hydrological processes. Study focus Conventional SWAT-based land-use studies often apply extreme land-use scenarios and oversimplify landscape heterogeneity. Terraces are treated as static BMPs with fixed Curve Number (CN), ignoring rainfall-driven CN variations and lowering simulation accuracy in terrace-dominated loess regions. This study uses realistic spatial land-use configurations instead of extreme scenarios and improves SWAT via slope-based terrace delineation and rainfall-intensity-dependent dynamic-CN calibration to evaluate land-use hydrological impacts and the conditional applicability of dynamic CN. New hydrological insights for the region The 2000 land-use dataset yields the best model performance (NSE = 0.8837, R² = 0.8865, PBIAS = −7.83%), superior to 2010 and 2020 datasets. Grassland expansion reduces runoff by 12.97%, much higher than the 2.49% from forest expansion, and urban expansion produces unstable interannual runoff responses. The dynamic-CN method improves daily-runoff simulation under drought and heavy-rainfall conditions, whereas static CN works better under mild stable rainfall. Terraces redistribute surface runoff into subsurface flow and baseflow with little impact on annual total runoff.

title: A progressive early warning system for flash drought based on meteorological precursors: A case study of the Dongjiang River Basin, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Qiang Huang, Lan Kong, Shaofeng Li, Shuyun Yuan, Xiaoshan Luo, Liao Ouyang, Peng Li
abstract: Study region The Dongjiang River Basin in southeast China, a critical water source region for the Pearl River Delta with a subtropical monsoon climate and frequent dry–wet transitions. Study focus Flash droughts threaten water and food security due to rapid onset, yet operational warnings remain largely single-indicator based. This study developed a progressive early warning system using pentad-scale ERA5-Land root-zone soil moisture (1950–2025). Precursors were screened through collinearity diagnosis, time-lag correlation, and random forest importance, followed by Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis, with predictive skill quantified by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) to determine warning thresholds within a two-stage regression-to-classification framework. New hydrological insights for the region Five precursors spanning three pentads prior to onset were identified. A two-pentad-ahead precipitation anomaly (P lag2, AUC = 0.74) and a one-pentad-ahead anomaly (P lag1, AUC = 0.92) formed the main warning chain, issuing L1 and L2 alerts 2 and 1 pentads ahead, respectively. Three weaker precursors (P lag3, ET/PET lag3, T lag2; all AUC ≈ 0.5) were integrated into a three-category supporting-condition score (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH). The system achieved a false positive rate of 6.3% (training) and 8.5% (validation), substantially lower than single-indicator (16.5%–18.6%) and logistic regression (16.3%–22.3%) baselines, with a higher Heidke Skill Score (0.370 vs. 0.262–0.269). Results were robust across 10 flash drought definition parameter combinations, and application to the 2019 event demonstrated timely, coherent warnings with no false alarms.

title: Potential of source-reservoir thermal regulation to alleviate low-temperature constraints on winter water conveyance in the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Lijin Liu, Xu Zhang, Youcai Tuo, Yun Deng, Fan Yang
abstract: Study region The main canal of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, China, one of the world’s largest long-distance interbasin water transfer systems. Study focus Winter low-temperature conditions and ice hazards constrain the winter water conveyance capacity of long-distance water transfer canals, yet the role of source reservoirs in regulating downstream thermal conditions remains unclear. This study developed and validated a winter water temperature model for the main canal, achieving RMSE values below 0.6°C and R² values above 0.9. Scenario experiments were conducted to assess how source-reservoir water-level rise and increased diversion discharge affect longitudinal heat transport and low-temperature constraints at the canal tail. New hydrological insights for the region The Danjiangkou Reservoir acts as an active thermal regulation node rather than only a water-supply boundary. Increased diversion discharge enhanced heat transport efficiency, reduced the longitudinal temperature gradient by 19%, and shifted the 14°C isotherm 404.8 km northward. Reservoir water-level rise strengthened the headwork thermal boundary and mainly improved near-source thermal conditions. Under suitable discharge, reservoir-induced thermal gains could reach the canal tail about 1200 km downstream. Joint regulation reduced 0–4 °C low-temperature days at BJM by 12–24%, indicating its potential to alleviate low-temperature constraints and support further evaluation of winter water conveyance capacity.

title: Contrasting roles of human water use in soil and hydrological drought propagation in the mid-upper Huaihe River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yiting Zou, Xing Yuan, Chenyuan Li
abstract: Study region The mid-upper Huaihe River Basin (MU-HRB) in China is a region characterized by strong climate variability and intensive human water use. Study focus This study examines how irrigation and reservoir regulation influence drought propagation (DP) from meteorological drought (MD) to soil drought (SD) and hydrological drought (HD) over the MU-HRB. The newly developed Conjunctive Surface Subsurface Process model version 3 (CSSPv3) with explicit representation of irrigation water source constraints, is applied to quantify the impacts of human water use on DP. The CSSPv3 model outperforms global hydrological models in terms of streamflow and soil moisture simulations over the MU-HRB. New hydrological insights for the region Human water use alters DP by modifying both pathways and thresholds. Irrigation suppresses SD, reducing its frequency by 58.8% and prolonging propagation time by 101.7%, while intensifying HD, increasing its frequency by 48.6% and accelerating propagation from MD. Reservoir regulation partly offsets streamflow depletion but does not reverse the enhanced propagation toward HD. Consequently, propagation shifts from pathways toward SD to HD. Human water use weakens the propagation of low severity MD events to SD, while lowering the threshold for propagation to HD, indicating increased sensitivity of streamflow systems. These effects are strongest in sub-basins with intensive human water use, particularly in the Huaibin-Bengbu region, and are driven by soil moisture replenishment, enhanced evapotranspiration, and streamflow depletion.

title: Contrasting growing season water use efficiency in an abandoned drained peatland pasture and an adjacent natural bog in western Newfoundland
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yufei Wang, Asare Gyimah, Hongze Ma, Jianghua Wu
abstract: Study region An abandoned drained peatland pasture undergoing natural revegetation and an adjacent natural bog in the Robinsons peatland complex, western Newfoundland, Canada. Study focus Understanding how agricultural drainage affects ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE = gross primary productivity / evapotranspiration) is critical for managing water resources in cultivated peatlands. However, the relative roles of carbon uptake versus hydrological partitioning of water loss remain poorly quantified. This study compared a natural boreal bog with an adjacent drained peatland pasture using chamber-based flux measurements across plant functional types and microtopographic features. New hydrological insights Equal date mixed model estimates of GPP were 0.49 mg CO2 m−2 s−1 (95% CI 0.43–0.55) at the abandoned pasture and 0.13 (0.07–0.19) at the natural bog. Estimated WUE was 0.03 mg CO2 mg−1 H2O (0.03–0.04) and 0.006 (0.004–0.009), respectively, corresponding to a site ratio of 5.38 (3.58–8.09). Mean adjusted ET did not differ clearly between the named sites (pasture minus bog = −2.02 mg H2O m−2 s−1, 95% CI −5.84–1.79), although ET trajectories differed by date. At the pasture, ET remained positively associated with photosynthetically active radiation. The environmental relationships were supported for a collar-sensitive positive association between deeper water tables and WUE. The chamber measured total water-vapour flux and did not partition evaporation from transpiration. These results provide site-specific, hypothesis generating evidence and require multisite, multiyear confirmation.

title: Spatial heterogeneity analysis of climate driving factors for spatiotemporal changes in potential evapotranspiration based on Multi‐Scale Geographically Weighted Regression and Geographical Detector
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yali Ma, Zuirong Niu, Dongyuan Sun
abstract: Study region Hexi Corridor, a representative arid and semi-arid inland region, northwestern China. Study focus To overcome the limitations of previous studies in terms of the spatial heterogeneity of the driving factors influencing potential evapotranspiration (PET) changes, and to address the issue of spatial non-stationarity of PET caused by climatic factors, this study exploratively introduced the Geographical Detector (GD) and Multi-Scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR). We analyzed the spatial-temporal distribution pattern of PET in the Hexi Corridor region, and revealed the spatial heterogeneity distribution characteristics of the driving factors at the grid cell scale. At the same time, important climatic factors with significant influence were identified, as well as the dual-factor driving mechanism. New hydrological insights for the region PET showed an increasing trend from southeast to northwest, with a significant increase accounting for 18.08%, a non-significant increase accounting for 57.86%, and a non-significant decrease accounting for 24.06%. In most areas of the Hexi Corridor, PET showed an increasing trend (75.94%). The precipitation and wind speed are the main factors causing spatial variations in PET. Any interaction between two factors is manifested as bi-variable enhance and nonlinear-enhance. The synergy of the two factors can enhance the explanatory power of a single factor for the spatial differentiation of PET. The influence of elevation on PET has a global characteristic, while the influence of meteorological factors has a stronger local dependence. The PET in the northwest of the Hexi Corridor is significantly affected by wind speed and temperature, while in the central and eastern parts, it is significantly inhibited by precipitation and relative humidity. In the southeast, PET is positively promoted by the sunshine duration. In most areas of the Hexi Corridor (86.21%), PET will show a continuous increasing trend in the future, while in some local areas in the west and east (13.79%), there will be a continuous decreasing trend.

title: Sub-monthly volumetric evolution of the supraglacial lakes in Northeastern Greenland based on the topographic depression method
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Huihui Zhao, Baojin Qiao, Mingcheng Hu, Jikun Liu, Jing Li, Haiyan Liu, Xin Li
abstract: Study region Supraglacial lakes on the northeastern Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) during the melt seasons (May–September) from 2018 to 2025. Study focus This study develops a multi-parameter inversion framework for supraglacial lakes by integrating multi-source remote sensing data and machine learning. Using Landsat-8 multispectral bands and indices combined with ArcticDEM, a machine learning model is constructed to map the supraglacial lake area. Lake volume is estimated via the terrain depression method. The framework enables high-temporal-resolution (sub-monthly) monitoring of supraglacial lake area and volume over a decadal scale. A key innovation is the quantitative analysis of altitudinal shifts in the spatial distribution of supraglacial lakes at high temporal resolution, along with region-specific attribution of climatic drivers. New hydrological insights The inversion reveals that the coverage of supraglacial lakes in high-elevation regions increased from less than 10–25% during the study period. Quantitative climate attribution shows significant elevation‑dependent heterogeneity: in mid‑elevation regions, temperature‑driven surface meltwater flux contributes 42.45% to changes in supraglacial lake volume, surpassing precipitation as the dominant factor; in high‑elevation regions, snowmelt recharge and surface runoff inputs are the primary drivers. This framework provides a scientifically robust technical solution for sub‑monthly dynamic monitoring of supraglacial lakes, filling the gap in high‑frequency, long‑term hydrological observation on the GrIS.

title: Characteristics of soil moisture dynamics and recharge pattern in alpine meadows under nitrogen addition conditions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zongjie Li, Fang Liu, Bowen Wang, Yixuan Wang, Juan Gui, Xiaxia Li, Zexi Chen
abstract: Study region Alpine meadows in the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (Shaliu River Basin), a permafrost-affected cold region sensitive to nitrogen deposition and climate change. Study focus Nitrogen addition can alter soil structure and hydrological processes, yet its impacts on soil-water dynamics and source partitioning in alpine meadows remain unclear. A two-year field experiment (2023–2024) with four nitrogen levels (0, 5, 10, 15 g m⁻² yr⁻¹) was conducted. Stable isotopes (δ²H, δ¹⁸O), LC-excess, and End-Member Mixing Analysis (EMMA) were used to trace soil-water origin, infiltration pathways, and source contributions under varying nitrogen inputs. New hydrological insights for the region Nitrogen addition significantly shifted infiltration regimes from preferential flow under control conditions to piston-flow dominance under N5 (May and July-September) and sustained piston flow under N10-N15 (June-September). (2) Precipitation supplied 34–46% of soil water, while underground ice and supra-permafrost water each contributed 26–33%, with seasonal switching from precipitation dominance (May-July) to increased frozen-ground inputs (August-September). (3) Higher nitrogen enhanced late-season supra-permafrost contributions and altered evapotranspiration partitioning. (4) Moderate nitrogen input (5 g m⁻² yr⁻¹) most effectively maintained piston-flow-dominated infiltration, enhanced deep percolation, and stabilized soil-water interactions, whereas excessive nitrogen reduced water-use efficiency and altered source contributions.

title: Application of an ANN model integrating station network distribution and water level increment principle in flood season water level prediction of Taihu Lake basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhongtian Zhang, Hao Qin, Qiang Xu, Huiming Zhang, Xinyi Wu, Li Liu, Yong Min, Xu Zhang, Wenhai Yang, Qinghua Liang
abstract: Study region The Taihu Lake basin is a typical plain river network area in eastern China, characterized by extremely gentle terrain, dense river-lake systems, intensive human activities, and complex hydrological interactions. The region is highly vulnerable to flooding during the flood season due to its flat landscape, concentrated rainfall. Study focus This study constructs controlled BP-ANN models with the spatial distribution of hydrological stations and real-time water level increment information. Five ablation BP-ANN models are established to quantify the contributions of water level increment, PLS fusion and multi-station data. SHAP method was adopted to interpret outputs for level prediction. The core focus is to find reliable method to improve water level prediction under complex hydrological conditions, reduce peak errors, and enhance the reliability of regional flood forecasting systems. New hydrological insights for the region Among all developed models, the single-station method provides the optimal compromise between prediction performance and model complexity. The multi-station method yields accuracy gains only for a small subset of stations with strong hydrological connectivity and introduces redundant features for most plain-river-network sites. The upstream and mid-plain areas show different confluence patterns affected by runoff and backwater. The findings support zoned intelligent forecasting for plain river networks, and can serve as a reliable way for flood control and regional hydrological services in the plain river network regions.

title: Environmental thresholds and lagged rainfall effects on stem sap flow in dryland shelterbelt trees
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yali Jia, Yiben Cheng, Xinle Li, Zhiming Xin, Jingwen Li, Zixuan Yuan, Lixia Chu
abstract: Study region This study was conducted at Xinhua Forest Farm, located in the desert–oasis transition zone of the Ulan Buh Desert, northwestern China, where mean annual precipitation and evaporation are approximately 132 and 2032 mm, respectively. Sap flow of Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica, Ulmus pumila, and Elaeagnus angustifolia was monitored during the 2024–2025 growing seasons. Study focus Generalized additive mixed models and distributed lag non-linear models were used to quantify nonlinear sap-flow responses to solar radiation (SR), vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and soil water content (SWC), and to assess lagged rainfall effects under different antecedent soil-moisture conditions. New hydrological insights for the region Cumulative sap flow was 1189.44, 1313.75, and 1849.44 kg for P. sylvestris, U. pumila, and E. angustifolia, respectively. Sap flow responded nonlinearly to all three environmental drivers (P < 0.001). The SR turning points were 323.0, 323.0, and 333.1 W m⁻²; the VPD turning points were 2.814, 1.763, and 2.223 kPa; and the SWC turning points were 0.0810, 0.0968, and 0.0586 m³ m⁻³ , respectively. Post-rainfall responses lasted 2–4 h in P. sylvestris, approximately 10 h in U. pumila, and more than 15 h in E. angustifolia. Their magnitude and duration depended strongly on antecedent SWC. These findings show that rainfall use by shelterbelt trees is jointly regulated by species-specific environmental thresholds and antecedent soil moisture.

title: Stability amidst variability: Four decades of hydrologic response in the Upper Snake River Basin, Wyoming, USA
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Zhufeng Fang, Fabian Nippgen, Ginger B. Paige, Salar Jarhan
abstract: Study region Mountain headwater basins are critical water sources, yet their long-term hydrologic response is often difficult to evaluate because observations are spatially sparse. This study examines the approximately 8900 km² Upper Snake River Basin in Wyoming, USA, a snowmelt-dominated headwater region supplying Jackson Lake and the broader Snake River system. Study focus We combined a 38-year WRF-Hydro simulation for WY 1984–2021 with observations from 15 U.S. Geological Survey gauges to evaluate seasonal runoff behavior, runoff efficiency, runoff timing, variation in gauge-network trends, and streamflow persistence. The model used a 300 m land-surface grid and a 30 m routing grid and achieved Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency values of 0.91 during calibration and 0.80 during evaluation. New hydrological insights for the region Runoff remained strongly concentrated in late spring and early summer, with most interannual variability occurring during the snowmelt season. At Flagg Ranch, annual runoff efficiency and cumulative runoff timing indicated no statistically detectable monotonic shifts, and the estimated runoff-ratio trends were much smaller than the changes the 38-year record could reliably detect. Across the 15-gauge network, significant trends were limited and not consistent across the basin, although localized responses occurred in regulated and hydro-geologically complex watersheds. Perennial channels remained the dominant and spatially persistent component of the modeled network, while seasonal and ephemeral reaches were concentrated in smaller headwater branches. Together, these findings reveal strong seasonal organization, localized hydrologic complexity, and persistent network structure amid substantial interannual variability, without pervasive directional hydrologic reorganization over the 1984–2021 period.

title: Revealing the mixed driving mechanism of hydrological disaster risk in the Dongting Lake Basin based on an improved risk index
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Pai Liu, Feng Li, Qianqian He, Yonghong Xie, Mingming Geng, Bikram Manandhar, Heng Jiang, Yue Xu, Siyuan Yue, Yuhe Zhang, Xin Weng
abstract: Study region Dongting Lake Basin, China Study focus This study focuses on assessing basin-scale hydrological disaster risk and disentangling its underlying mixed driving mechanisms. Two core objectives are defined: (1) assessing basin-scale hydrological disaster risk through satellite-derived surface water observations, and (2) quantifying the individual and combined contributions of climate variability, economic development, and vegetation dynamics to hydrological disaster risk. We develop a hybrid framework for basin-scale hydrological disaster risk assessment, which integrates satellite imagery, spectral water indices (including NDWI, MNDWI, and SPWI), and machine learning algorithms. Further, we conducted multiple attribution analysis using multiple linear regression and SHAP interpretation analysis based on random forest to quantify the long-term driving mechanism of hydrological disaster risk. New hydrological insights for the region This study found the hydrological disaster risk in the Dongting Lake Basin has shown inconsistent trends, with an overall decreasing trend. In the study area, approximately 79.56% of the basin experienced a reduction in risk, while 20.44% exhibited an increase. The increase in risk is related to the increase in precipitation within the basin and the transition of land use from forest areas to farmland. However, changes in GDP, land use changes, and vegetation greening offset the hydrological disaster risks caused by increased precipitation in most regions. These findings provide a scientific foundation for water resource management and hydrological risk mitigation strategies.

title: Lake–aquifer connectivity controls groundwater dynamics in a multi-aquifer system within a typical floodplain
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hanxiao Wang, Fu Liao, Guangcai Wang, Xianglong Chen, Ziwen Zhang, Luoyao Xiong, Peng Sun, Yongzhen Fu
abstract: Study region The study was conducted in the Poyang Lake floodplain, China, where a vertically stratified multi-aquifer system interacts with Poyang Lake, a seasonal lake (Candou Lake), regional lateral flow, rainfall infiltration, and artificial ponds. Study focus This study investigates the drivers of groundwater level dynamics in a vertically stratified aquifer system at small spatial scale (<30 m). High-frequency groundwater monitoring, cross-correlation analysis, wavelet analysis, and numerical groundwater flow modeling were integrated to identify aquifer-specific responses to hydrological and anthropogenic controls. New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater dynamics presented pronounced vertical heterogeneity within < 30 m. The shallow aquifer was mainly controlled by rainfall infiltration and Candou Lake recharge. The intermediate aquifer was connected to both Candou Lake and Poyang Lake, but Candou Lake exerted stronger control during the flood period. The deep aquifer was alternately influenced by Poyang Lake recharge and regional lateral flow: the lake recharge initiates groundwater rise, whereas lateral recharge controlled peak groundwater levels. Model simulations confirmed that Candou Lake provides greater recharge to the shallow and intermediate aquifers than rainfall and Poyang Lake, respectively, while Poyang Lake initially dominated recharge to the deep aquifer. Artificial ponds elevated groundwater levels in shallow and intermediate aquifers, maintained high levels during the dry season, and enhanced local recharge. These findings highlight the necessity of high-resolution, multi-aquifer characterization to support groundwater management in floodplains.

title: Intercomparison of precipitation frequency estimates derived from high-resolution weather radar and rain gauge measurements in Zealand, Denmark
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Ida Kemppinen Vester, Janni Mosekær Nielsen, Jesper Ellerbæk Nielsen, Søren Thorndahl
abstract: Study region: Zealand, Denmark. Study focus: Precipitation frequency estimates (PFEs) guide the design of urban drainage systems by specifying return periods for pluvial flooding. PFEs are typically derived from point rainfall measurements, whereas weather radar provides spatially distributed precipitation measurements. This study compares PFEs and PFE model parameters derived from weather radar and rain gauge data at timescales from 1 min to 48 h, with a focus on spatial variability. PFEs are estimated empirically with the median plotting position and parametrically using a Peaks-Over-Threshold approach, generating partial duration series modeled by the Generalized Pareto distribution. New hydrological insights for the region: Return levels from weather radar and rain gauges often exhibit increasing agreement at durations above approximately 200–300 min, depending on the estimation method and return period considered. At short timescales, rain gauges show higher mean exceedances μ and thresholds z 0 than radar pixels, while yearly exceedance rates λ and shapes κ are more consistent between the data sets. Results at the shortest timescales are, however, associated with greater uncertainty. Spatial gradients are found for λ . Spatial autocorrelation of return levels, κ , and μ increases with increasing rainfall duration, while spatial autocorrelation for λ remains high for all timescales considered. Differences in PFEs and model parameters likely stem from inherent differences in measurement techniques and spatial scales between the weather radar and rain gauge data.

title: Distribution and source apportionment of groundwater nitrate contamination in shallow and deep aquifers of the Hebei Plain: A combined interpretation of PCA-APCS-MLR, hydrochemical methods, and land use characteristics
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Pan Bi, Manni Chao, Ruinan Liu, Guanxing Huang, Zhichao Li, Ziting Yuan
abstract: Study region Hebei Plain, China Study focus Groundwater nitrate contamination is a global concern, and methods for its source apportionment are generally complicated. This study aims to investigate the distribution of nitrate in shallow and deep groundwater across different land use types in the Hebei Plain, and to estimate the relative contributions of potential nitrate sources via the integration of principal component analysis-absolute principal component score-multiple linear regression (PCA-APCS-MLR), conventional hydrochemical methods, and land use information. New hydrological insights for the region Proportions of high-nitrate (> 50 mg/L) groundwater (PHNG) in shallow aquifers in both of piedmont and littoral plains were 5 times or more that in shallow aquifer of the central plain and deep aquifer of various sub-plains. In the piedmont plain, PHNGs in shallow aquifers in both of bare and urban lands were more than 50%, followed by woods-grasslands (43.8%), agricultural lands (27.6%), and rural areas (18.8%); by contrast, the PHNG in deep aquifers in urban lands was 40% and > 10 times that in other land use types. In the central plain, the PHNG in shallow aquifers in rural areas was > 9 times that in agricultural lands. This is opposite to the littoral plain where the PHNGs in shallow aquifers in agricultural lands was 1.6 times that in rural areas. The relative contribution results calculated by PCA-APCS-MLR suggest that manure and septic sewage are preliminarily inferred as the dominant potential sources (58.8%) of nitrate in shallow groundwater of the piedmont plain, followed by mixed sources (25.8%), fertilizers (11.7%), natural sources (2.3%), as well as domestic sewage and nitrification in vadose zones (1.4%). A considerable proportion of mixed sources for groundwater nitrate in the piedmont plain indicates that overlapping nitrogen sources cannot be fully separated by the PCA-APCS-MLR model. In contrast, fertilizers (40.6%) and manure (37.7%) are inferred to be the two major contributors to nitrate in shallow groundwater of the littoral plain. This study reveals that the combination of PCA-APCS-MLR, conventional hydrochemical methods and land use information serves as a cost-effective approach to assess source contributions of groundwater nitrate in large alluvial plains such as the Hebei Plain. It should be noted that this method has limitations in distinguishing overlapping nitrogen sources, and the results require comprehensive interpretation.

title: A multiscale dynamic network-based method for radar precipitation nowcasting: A case study in the Yiluo River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yingrui Li, Qiting Zuo, Tao Li, Yihu Ji
abstract: Study region Yiluo River Basin, China Study focus Accurate and timely precipitation nowcasting is essential for mitigating rainstorms and floods. This study proposes a Multiscale Dynamic Nowcasting Network (MDN-Net) that integrates temporal and motion features for radar echo extrapolation and quantitative precipitation estimation. A four-dimensional evaluation framework is also developed to comprehensively assess nowcasting performance from multiple perspectives. New hydrological insights for the region (1) MDN-Net significantly improves strong echo extrapolation and outperforms the other models at lead times of 1.5–2 h. (2) For quantitative precipitation estimation, MDN-Net accurately captures the observed temporal evolution of rainfall, although cumulative precipitation is slightly overestimated. It achieves the smallest RBIAS magnitude (-2.05% to −3.51%), indicating superior robustness and generalization capability. (3) Module analysis demonstrates that MDN-Net with the feature fusion module maintains stable performance across thresholds and lead times. Specifically, F1-score increases by 44.3% and 35.1% at 1.5 h and 2 h lead times compared with U-Net and Flow U-Net, respectively. Overall, by integrating temporal sequence and motion features, MDN-Net provides a more comprehensive and accurate representation of precipitation systems, significantly enhances spatiotemporal perception, and improves nowcasting performance, offering a promising framework for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of precipitation nowcasting and supporting disaster prevention and water resource management.

title: Uncovering the impact of catchment attributes in regionalized models through explainable artificial intelligence
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Xianghuan Kong, Shanhu Jiang, Chunsheng Yang, Miao He, Bang Yang, Jiabin Zhang, Mao Li, Liliang Ren
abstract: Study region 531 ungauged basins in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Study focus: We propose XNLSTM, an interpretive framework combining regionalized Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) modeling, 10-fold basin cross-validation, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, including Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), the Morris method, and permutation feature importance (PFI), to examine how catchment attributes affect runoff prediction in ungauged basins. The framework jointly uses multiple XAI methods to reveal interpretational variability and identify catchment attributes with relatively stable importance across methods. It then trains models under different catchment attribute configurations derived from the XAI-based interpretation results and interprets fold-specific models to assess the stability of catchment attribute importance across basin splits and configurations. New hydrological insights for the region: SHAP, Morris, and PFI produce different rankings for the same LSTM model, but p_mean, aridity, and other catchment attributes remain consistently important. Across the three XAI rankings, climatic and topographic attributes are consistently more important than soil, geological, and vegetation attributes for overall runoff prediction. Using more catchment attributes, and using attributes with higher XAI-derived importance, improves cross-basin generalization. However, lower ranked attribute combinations show slight tendencies to reproduce low-flow and high-flow metrics closer to observations. Importance rankings are relatively stable for all-attribute models but change more clearly when models use attribute subsets. Attributes such as elev_mean, pet_mean, and soil_conductivity remain important across basin splits and configurations.

title: Responses of seasonal baseflow to climate warming in an alpine mountain basin: Insights from GAMLSS modeling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Bing Bai, Ping Wang, Shiqi Liu, Mingming Feng, Yichi Zhang, Tingting Wang, Qiwei Huang, Irina S. Danilovich, Sergey P. Pozdniakov
abstract: Study region The Kaidu River is a cryosphere-fed inland river in the central Tianshan Mountains of arid northwest China, sustaining downstream oases, irrigated agriculture, and Bosten Lake. Study focus We examined seasonal baseflow responses to warming during 1961–2020 and an abrupt regime shift. Daily streamflow for 2009–2020 was reconstructed with a Long Short-Term Memory model, baseflow was separated using nine methods centered on the Eckhardt filter, and monthly controls were quantified with Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape. New hydrological insights for the region Baseflow averaged 77.6 m3/s (68% of streamflow), indicating strong groundwater buffering by the Quaternary aquifer. Around 1996, annual streamflow and baseflow increased by 24% and 22%, respectively, and the shift was reproduced by all nine methods. Antecedent wetness was significant from April to November, revealing persistent groundwater memory. Climate–baseflow coupling followed four seasonal phases: storage-dominated spring, climate-sensitive summer, storage-controlled autumn recession, and an early-winter transition. Over 1961–2020, a 1°C increase in temperature was associated with 8.6% higher July baseflow; stratified analyses further showed that temperature emerged as a significant July driver only after 1996. These findings reveal strong groundwater memory and an increasing influence of warming on warm-season baseflow, with implications for downstream water supply in the Yanqi Basin.

title: Optimal distribution functions for drought characterization across Europe’s climatic gradient
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Babak Mohammadi, Wei Yang, Majid Cheraghalizadeh, Ilias Pechlivanidis
abstract: Study region This study focuses on pan-European climatic regimes, evaluating drought characterization at the Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics level (NUTS-3). Study focus Accurate statistical characterization of drought events is essential for effective water resources management and disaster risk reduction, yet the selection of appropriate probability distributions remains uncertain under regional climatic diversity. This study develops a rigorous methodological framework for optimizing drought characterization through systematic probability distribution function (PDF) selection. Eight candidate PDFs were evaluated for characterizing meteorological and hydrological drought. We calculated the standardized precipitation index (SPI-3), standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI-3), and standardized streamflow index (SSI-3) at 3-month timescale using L-moments for parameter estimation. A two-stage selection process was then applied, using the Anderson-Darling test and corrected Akaike Information Criterion. New hydrological insights for the region Results show optimal PDF selection is climate-dependent, indicator-specific, and seasonally variable. For SPI-3, the Gamma (GAM) distribution dominates across most European climate zones, validating conventional approaches for precipitation-based indices. SPEI-3 exhibits spatial heterogeneity, with the Pearson Type III being recommended for central and western European climates, and the Normal distribution for Scandinavia and Mediterranean regions. SSI-3 is the most spatially variable, with LN3 recommended across central and western Europe, GAM for northern Scandinavia and parts of the Mediterranean, and GEV in the Baltic region and scattered coastal and southern regions.

title: Multi-isotope tracing reveals nitrate and sulfate sources and fate across contrasting activity zones in a semi-arid basin of northern China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chang Yue, Ruizhong Gao, Limin Duan, Tianke Su, Xixi Wang, Tingxi Liu, Guoqiang Wang
abstract: Study region The Dahei River Basin, a semi-arid basin in northern China. Study focus In semi-arid surface water-groundwater systems, nitrate (NO3 –) and sulfate (SO4 2–) are jointly influenced by natural processes and anthropogenic activities, yet how their sources, transformations, and export vary across contrasting activity zones remains insufficiently understood. Integrating hydrochemistry, multiple stable isotopes, a Bayesian isotope mixing model, and representative-section flux analysis, this study investigated the source compositions, transformation processes, and export differences of NO3 – and SO4 2– in the Dahei River Basin. New hydrological insights for the region: Results showed greater SO4 2– enrichment in high-activity zones, whereas NO3 – exceedance was more prominent in low-activity zones. In low-activity areas, NO3 – mainly originated from manure and sewage (35.2%) and soil organic nitrogen (27.7%), whereas high-activity areas showed more mixed NO3 – sources. For SO4 2–, sulfide oxidation and manure and sewage were major sources in both zones, contributing 29.8–36.6% and 24.0–24.8%, respectively. Nitrification dominated NO3 – transformation, whereas SO4 2– transformation reflected overlapping effects of sulfide oxidation and mineralization, together with contributions from evaporite dissolution. At nested sections in the low and high activity zones, downstream annual cumulative NO3 – and SO4 2– fluxes were 3.16 and 8.41 times the upstream values, respectively, reflecting flow accumulation and combined natural and anthropogenic influences. These findings support zone-based source control and tailored water environment management in semi-arid basins.

title: Widespread intensification of rainfall erosivity over the Loess Plateau in a warmer world
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Chu-Nan Zhang, Meng-Zhuo Zhang, Weidong Guo
abstract: Study region The Loess Plateau of China hosts the world’s most extensive and thickest loess deposits. The porous, fragile loess and complex climate cause severe soil erosion here, making it one of the most severely eroded areas in the world. Study focus The rainfall erosivity (RE) serves as the active factor that leads to its change. This study assesses future changes in RE across the region based on 23 sets of statistical downscaling datasets under three SSP-RCP scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicate that over 97% of the region will experience significantly increased RE, following a northwest-to-southeast increasing gradient, and areas with historically high RE intensify the most. Regarding the regional mean, annual RE is projected to rise by 25.7%, 21.9%, and 27.8% during 2041–2070 against 1985–2014 under SSP1‐2.6, SSP2‐4.5, and SSP5‐8.5, respectively. By 2071–2100, these values will reach 24.2%, 28.3%, and 53.5%. Seasonally, May and September will contribute most to the annual increase. The projected RE increase is dominated by more frequent and intense moderate and heavy rainfall. These findings reveal a shifting erosion regime across the Loess Plateau, with potential impacts on ecosystem stability, water resource distribution, and flood risk management. This regional assessment could provide a basis for evaluating future risks and for developing integrated strategies for soil conservation, water resources management, and ecosystem protection under a changing climate.

title: Event-based hydrological processes and sediment yield at semi-arid catchments of Northern Ethiopia
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Gebremeskel Teklay Berhe, Berhane Grum, Coen J. Ritsema, Jantiene E.M. Baartman
abstract: Study region Two adjacent small catchments located upstream of a reservoir-based irrigation system in the highlands of northern Ethiopia, characterized by semi-arid climate conditions. Soil erosion causes socioeconomic and ecological disturbances. Reservoir sedimentation is among the negative off-site effects of soil erosion. Study Focus The discharge-suspended sediment concentration hysteresis pattern was analyzed. An event-based hydrological model, OpenLISEM was also applied in small, paired catchments to evaluate the effectiveness of soil and water conservation measures in reducing sediment yield and reservoir sedimentation. Rainfall events were calibrated independently due to differences of model parameters between storm events. New hydrological insights for the region Initial soil moisture content was found to be the most sensitive parameter affecting simulated peak and total discharge. OpenLISEM performed satisfactorily for most of the calibrated events in capturing peak discharge and discharge hydrograph. Complex hysteresis patterns were observed during heavy rainfall events with multiple discharge peaks. The results indicate that implementing stone bunds on hillslopes together with check dams across gully channels reduces sediment yield at both catchment outlets by 36–74% relative to the calibrated baseline scenarios. The findings provide valuable insight for the potential of different soil and water conservation measures to reduce sediment yield and reservoir sedimentation, contributing to the long-term sustainability of reservoir-based irrigation schemes in the semi-arid highlands of northern Ethiopia.

title: Fault-controlled hydrogeochemical spatial evolution revealed by machine learning around the 2010 Ms 7.1 Yushu earthquake zone
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hongyi He, Zhi Chen, Qingyong Luo, Bihong Fu, Zihan Gao, Yili Luo, Zhikeng Huang, Zhaofei Liu, Ke Zhang, Weiye Shao, Ying Li
abstract: Study Region: The Ganzi-Yushu fault zone (GYFZ) is an active strike-slip fault on the eastern Tibetan Plateau, separating the Bayan Har and Qiangtang blocks. Study Focus: Active strike-slip faults can act as barriers and conduits for groundwater, making them important settings for understanding how seismic deformation redistributes meteoric recharge and deep volatiles. In the GYFZ, along-strike fault coupling, the 2010 Yushu rupture, and heterogeneous lithologies require clarification of how fault architecture controls groundwater circulation and hydrochemical differentiation. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Hydrochemical, water-isotope, gas-isotope, and unsupervised machine-learning evidence (Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)) from 31 water samples and 9 gas-sampling sites shows the GYFZ is compartmentalized. Stable isotopes indicate meteoric recharge, but circulation is partitioned by mechanical state. Highly coupled locked sectors preserve dilute meteoric Cluster 2 waters and limit vertical exchange with deep fluids. Ruptured and coupling-transition domains provide conduits for deeper, warmer Cluster 1 fluids, producing SiO2, Na+, Cl-, and HCO3 - enrichment and variable volatile input (CO2 = 1.02–99.04%; Rc = 0.10–0.51 Ra). Cluster 3, represented by GQNY, records a local sulfate-rich flow path through evaporitic and carbonate lithologies; its SO4 2- enrichment reflects mineral availability and hydrological connectivity rather than CO2-driven acidity. Thus, fault coupling determines conduit-barrier behaviour, whereas lithology controls the reaction fingerprint, explaining localized volatile-bearing anomalies along the fault.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and hydroclimatic contributions associated with drought–flood abrupt alternation in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Ying Xue, Lei Zou, Jun Xia, Chengjian Liu, Si Hong
abstract: Study region Yangtze River Basin of China Study focus This study examines the spatiotemporal patterns, seasonality, periodic variability, and hydroclimatic contributions of drought–flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) in the Yangtze River Basin during 1961–2023. Drought-to-flood (DF) and flood-to-drought (FD) events are identified using a standardized DFAA index (DFAAI) constructed from consecutive monthly standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) values. Trend, hotspot, spectral, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses assess their frequency, intensity, evolution, and associated predictors. New hydrological insights for the region DFAA frequency and intensity exhibit distinct spatial patterns, indicating that the recurrence and severity of rapid water-balance reversals are not spatially uniform across the Yangtze River Basin. High-frequency areas occur mainly in the middle–lower basin and lake regions, exceeding 10 events per decade, whereas the strongest events cluster along the Sichuan Basin margin. Basin-mean linear trends are weak, but DFAA variability strengthened after 2000. DF events span June–October, while FD events concentrate in July–September and show stronger synchronization among sub-basins, reflecting different monsoon-season pathways of moisture recovery and depletion. DF and FD frequencies show recurrent 3–5-year variability, whereas intensity contains longer-period components. SHAP results indicate that rapid precipitation and humidity changes are most consistently associated with the initiation of water-balance reversals, while temperature and radiation conditions contribute more strongly to their intensity, especially for FD. Large-scale circulation indices mainly modulate the background climate state.

title: A cascaded deep learning framework for improved forecasting of drought-flood abrupt alternation events in the Hanjiang River Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yubing Wang, Si Chen, Kedi Fang, Tiancheng Wang, Heng Hu, Rui Xia, Min Wang, Hai Liu
abstract: Study region The Hanjiang River Basin (HJRB), a meteorologically and topographically complex region in China. Study focus Drought-Flood Abrupt Alternation (DFAA) events threaten water security, yet their prediction remains challenging because of highly nonlinear dynamics and pronounced zero inflation in meteorological records. This study employed the Standardized Drought-Wetness Abrupt Alternation Index (SDWAI) to identify DFAA events and used SHAP to reveal their driving mechanisms. A cascaded framework integrating a parallel convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) classifier, wavelet decomposition, and ensemble regression was developed. By separating event identification from conditional intensity estimation, the framework reduced the influence of non-event samples. New hydrological insights for the region The CNN-LSTM classifier achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.67 and module obtained the best performance (R² = 0.91). The complete cascade framework achieved an overall R² of 0.58 and reduced the peak underestimation commonly observed in conventional zero-inflated regression models. Spatiotemporal analysis revealed distinct phase-locking characteristics of DFAA events, with downstream and southeastern HJRB identified as hazard hotspots. Drought to flood transitions occurred mainly during spring and summer, whereas flood-to-drought transitions increased markedly during late autumn and early winter. Local precipitation and potential evapotranspiration dominated DFAA evolution, while the Arctic Oscillation primarily regulated the large-scale atmospheric circulation background. These findings demonstrate the potential of cascaded deep learning frameworks for regional DFAA forecasting and adaptive water resource management.

title: Influence of salt concentration in the drying Lake Urmia on the saltwater intrusion
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Hojjat Ahmadi, Mohammad Hemmati, Somayeh Hejabi
abstract: Study region Lake Urmia and its adjacent coastal aquifer in northwestern Iran, a region that has experienced substantial lake shrinkage over recent decades. Study focus Lake desiccation has increased salinity and water density while lowering lake levels, introducing competing controls on saltwater intrusion into surrounding aquifers. This study quantifies the combined effects of lake level decline and salinity-driven density changes over two decades using a density-dependent SEAWAT model, calibrated and validated against groundwater observations. New hydrological insights for the region Assuming constant lake water density results in a slight advance followed by retreat of the saltwater wedge. In contrast, incorporating observed density increases produces significant wedge expansion, reaching up to 270% of its initial length (from 195 to 540 m) despite a > 6 m decline in lake level. Sensitivity analysis indicated that saltwater intrusion is generally more responsive to changes in groundwater and lake hydraulic heads than to density variations. However, in Lake Urmia, declines in lake level and groundwater level largely counterbalanced each other, reducing the net hydraulic-gradient effect and leaving the increase in lake-water density as the primary driver of wedge expansion. These findings demonstrate that density effects can dominate over hydraulic gradients in shrinking saline lakes under such conditions, accelerating groundwater salinization. The results highlight the necessity of incorporating density variations in modeling and provide critical insight for sustainable groundwater management in arid regions affected by saline lake drying.

title: Impacts of tropical cyclones on episodic transport of water and suspended sediment in mountainous catchments: A case study from Hainan Island
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Caifeng Liu, Wei Jiang, Shanshan Deng, Yangyang Yong, Tingwu Gu, Yuchen Shi, Siqi Du, Ting Yang, Kefu Yu
abstract: Study region Hainan Island, China, focusing on three major rivers: the Nandu, Changhua, and Wanquan River basins. Study focus Tropical cyclones (TCs) are key drivers of episodic riverine material fluxes in coastal mountainous regions. However, their quantitative role in regulating water discharge and suspended sediment discharge (SSD) in tropical island basins remains poorly constrained. Based on 64 years (1960–2023) of daily hydrological records, this study quantifies TC-associated contributions to water discharge and SSD and examines how TCs modify water–sediment transport. New hydrological insights for the region Quantitative analysis indicates that TCs exert a substantial influence on water discharge and SSD, contributing 4 ± 4% to 8 ± 6% of annual water discharge and 11 ± 10% to 30 ± 27% of annual SSD on average, with contributions reaching 91–95% of SSD in extreme years. Their influence on SSD is markedly stronger than on water discharge, indicating a pronounced sediment-routing enhancement. Sensitivity to TC forcing varies substantially across basins and these inter-basin differences are jointly regulated by TC characteristics, basin geomorphology (such as area and slope), and reservoir regulation. The identified water–sediment response regimes further highlight the nonlinear nature of sediment transport under TC forcing. These findings refine the understanding of extreme-event-driven material fluxes and provide a critical basis for managing flood risks, reservoir operations, and soil conservation in tropical island river systems.

title: Quantifying precipitation-induced changes in the proportion of nitrate inputs and their role in karst processes: Evidence from stable isotopes and water chemistry
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Wei Zhang, Zhongfa Zhou, Hui Dong, Jijuan Wang, Yi Huang, Xiaoduo Wang, Huijing Wei, Yang Bai, Mingyang An
abstract: Study region The study region is located within Shuanghe Cave National Geopark, China. Study focus Global warming has intensified extreme rainfall events, yet existing carbon cycle models generally overlook nitric acid weathering processes modulated by rainfall, leading to biased estimates of karst carbon sinks. In this study, conventional physicochemical parameters of water bodies, δ15N- NO 3 − , δ18O- NO 3 − and δ13C-DIC were measured simultaneously. Using the MixSIAR model, we distinguished the dynamic changes in nitrate source contributions before and after rainstorms, quantitatively estimated the proportion of carbonate weathering driven by nitric acid, elucidated the mechanism by which intensive rainfall-driven nitrogen input reduces the karst carbon sink, and corrected the biases inherent in traditional karst carbon-sink assessment methods. New hydrological insights After heavy rainfall, the proportion of anthropogenic nitrate increased markedly - by 37% in June and 22.4% in October - with higher nitrogen leaching intensity in June (agriculturally dominated) than in October (domestic-pollution dominated). Notably, the overall proportion of carbonate weathering attributed to nitric acid declined following rainstorms: from 8.24% to 7.14% in June, and from 4.96% to 3.56% in October. Under heavy storm conditions (daily rainfall ≥ 50 mm), the contribution of nitric acid to carbonate weathering is weakened by rainwater dilution. Therefore, for shallow karst watersheds, it is unwarranted to categorically conclude that rainfall promotes nitric-acid-mediated carbonate weathering; instead, the evaluation framework for weathering processes and carbon-sink effects should be further refined under different rainfall intensity scenarios.

title: Synchronously considering spatial dependence and temporal persistence into a deep learning based method for improving soil moisture spatial resolution
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Yanqing Yang, Jinqian Xia, Zhenxin Bao, Jiujiang Wu, Wei Zhao
abstract: Study region The Huai River Basin is a major agricultural region in central-eastern China, characterized by a monsoon climate, strong seasonal precipitation variability, and frequent drought–flood alternation. High-resolution soil moisture (SM) information is therefore essential for regional hydrological applications. Study focus A hybrid convolutional long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) framework was developed to downscale the European Space Agency Climate Change Initiative (ESA CCI) SM product. Meteorological, vegetation, and topographic predictors were integrated, while ESA CCI data and dense in situ observations jointly constrained model training. Predictor combinations, model structures, and target resolutions were systematically evaluated. CNN–LSTM outperformed CNN-only and LSTM-only models, achieving an overall correlation of approximately 0.79 and an unbiased root mean square error (ubRMSE) of 0.041 m³/m³. Extended triple collocation showed that the 5 km product reached a median correlation of 0.91 and a median RMSE of 0.018 m³/m³, outperforming ERA5 and SMAP. New hydrological insights for the region Multi-day accumulated precipitation explained SM variability better than daily rainfall, indicating clear antecedent-rainfall memory. Precipitation mainly controlled wetting–drying transitions, whereas vegetation and terrain regulated spatial redistribution and water retention. The lower accuracy at 1 km than at 5 km revealed scale dependence, suggesting that excessively fine downscaling may introduce unsupported spatial variability. Overall, the 5 km product more reliably preserved basin-scale SM gradients and seasonal dynamics.

title: Non-iterative coordination method for multi-objective flood control operation of a reservoir group based on equivalent projection theory
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 67 Author(s): Bin Wang, Yukun Fan, Xinyuan Qian, Chengjing Xu, Ran Mo, Sunyu Xu, Zixin Song, Yiwen Wang, Jieyu Li, Ping-an Zhong
abstract: Study region The middle Yellow River Basin (MYRB) Study focus In real-time flood control operation, high-dimensional nonlinear models challenge timely decision-making. Conventional iterative decomposition–coordination methods suffer from slow convergence in dimensionality reduction. This study proposes an efficient multi-reservoir flood control optimization method (EOM-EP) by coupling a non-iterative coordination framework based on equivalent projection theory (EP) with parallel computing. Numerical experiments demonstrate its accuracy and computational efficiency. Application to typical flood events in the MYRB further highlights upstream-downstream risk transfer mechanisms and flood regulation roles of mainstem and tributary reservoirs. New hydrological insights for the region (1) The non-iterative global coordination mechanism of EOM-EP is applicable to flood control operation of reservoir groups at different scales, and, compared with the Lagrange method, its performance becomes increasingly superior as the dimensionality of decision variables increases.
